title: wslua: Expose conversation API
description:
This merge request resolves #15396. A new Conversation object has been added that exposes the underlying C 'conversation' api.

The API is relatively complete, but for the sake of simplicity, I have not exposed any of the '_deinterlacer' functions, nor have I exposed 'elements' functions. These can come later.

For now, the extent of the API is as follows:
```lua
-- Functions to fetch conversations
local conv1 = Conversation.find_with_pinfo(pinfo, [options], [bool_create])
local conv2 = Conversation.find_by_id(frame_id, convtypes.<CONV_TYPE>, id, [bool_create])
local conv3 = Conversation.find(frame_id, convtypes.<CONV_TYPE>, addr1, port1, [addr2], [port2], [bool_create])
-- This last one is equivalent to calling Conversation.find_with_pinfo(pinfo)
local conv4 = pinfo.conversation

-- Set data
conv1[proto] = "asdf"
conv2[proto] = {"asdf": 123}

-- Get data
local data = conv3[proto]

-- Clear data
conv3[proto] = nil

-- Set dissector (equivalent to pinfo.conversation = <dissector>)
conv1.dissector = <dissector>
```

I'm not sure you need to register this conversation data at all. It's allocated in file scope, and there's a wmem callback that deletes it when the file scope ends. What is the point of registering it to the protocol?
Commenting out the registration does not seem to cause any leaks when running with ASAN (including with WIRESHARK_DEBUG_WMEM_OVERRIDE=simple).
!18941 just removes the code and relies upon the conversation data being freed when file scope leaves. I don't get any leaks that way.

Hm, ok.

The reason I added the extra registration was to deal with the case where `Action->Reload Lua Plugins` is executed from the GUI. If a Lua plugin is reloaded but conversation data isn't dealt with, the cd->data_ref field is no longer valid (as part of reloading plugins, the whole Lua state machine is deinited and reinited). That'll still be a dangling (although non-leaky) ref.

It might need a bit more thought on my end for a cleaner way of dealing with this. I'm open to suggestions for ways to handle this.

Regardless, I think you're right. It probably doesn't need to be registered to the `Protocol` at all.

So, FWIW, when Reload Lua Plugins is executed from the GUI, `WiresharkMainWindow::reloadLuaPlugins()` is called, and the file scope gets destroyed. It depends slightly on whether the current capture file was opened with a Lua FileHandler (in which case the file is closed and reopened) or not (in which case the file scope is left in `cf_redissect_packets()` - which happens after `wslua_reload_plugins`). I agree that it's possible that the `cd->data_ref` field might refer to something no longer valid when the file scope is destroyed. (Though loading the file and the script for your test from the GUI and executing Reload Lua Plugins didn't cause ASAN to complain.)

In the case where the file is `left` after `wslua_reload_plugins`, it seems luaL_unref is executed against the newly instantiated Lua state. I think this should be fine. When luaL_unref is called with an index that's never been set, it safely ignores the request to unref anything (basically treats them as no-ops).

I'm satisfied the way it is now should be fine.

However, I'll still do a commit to update the readme.
